title: The Gāyatrī (Sāvitrī): may Savitṛ impel our minds

words.role: points to bhargaḥ: ‘that splendour’; or, read as a genitive, ‘of him’
words.context: Bhāskara offers both: «तत् तस्य 'सुपां सुलुक्' इति षष्ठ्या लुक्», and later «तद् अन्नादि»
Bhāskara: «भर्गः तेजः अन्नं धनं वा»; in his last reading «पापानां तापनं तेजो मण्डलात्मकं», the light that burns away sin

words.gram: root aorist (or injunctive) optative sense, 1st pl. middle
words.meaning: may we hold, may we meditate on
words.context: Bhāskara: «धीमहि धारयेम», ‘may we hold’; or from √ध्यै, ‘we hold it in the mind’: «मनसा धारयामः»

words.role: subject of the relative clause: Savitṛ

words.meaning: may he impel, may he urge on

sandhi.rule: visarga after u becomes r before a voiced sound

morphology.note: the subjunctive (leṭ) of the causative of प्र-√चुद्, with the ā inserted by the Vedic rule Bhāskara cites; it expresses a wish.
Bhāskara derives it from √धी ‘to hold’ (a root aorist without augment) or, as many later teachers do, from √ध्यै ‘to meditate’.

translation.literal: That excellent splendour of the god Savitṛ may we hold — who shall impel our thoughts.
translation.readable: We meditate on the glorious light of the divine Savitṛ: may he inspire our minds.

meaning: The Gāyatrī, also called the Sāvitrī after its god: the verse given at the upanayana and repeated in every Sandhyā. It has three pādas of eight syllables. The worshipper holds in mind the radiance of Savitṛ, the god who sets everything in motion, and asks him to set the mind itself in motion — to impel and direct understanding. Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara reads it several ways: as a prayer for the god’s gifts, and finally as the instruction to meditate on the supreme light standing as the Sun, «सूर्यात्मना स्थितं पारमेश्वरं तेज उपास्यत्वेन उपदिश्यते». In the Taittirīya Saṃhitā it occurs at 1.5.6.4 and 4.1.11.1; in the Ṛgveda it is 3.62.10, a hymn of Viśvāmitra.
in_the_rite: The centre of the rite. Recited with the vyāhṛtis for each arghya (three in the morning and evening, fewer at midday, then one more for atonement), within the prāṇāyāma (with the praṇava, the seven vyāhṛtis and the ‘head’), and in the japa, repeated many times. The prayoga’s viniyoga: Viśvāmitra the seer, nicṛd gāyatrī the metre, Savitṛ the deity (vin-savitri; vin-arghya).

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara, on TS 1.5.6, first reads tat as a genitive and dhīmahi as ‘may we hold’: «वरणीयं सर्वैः प्रार्थनीयं भर्गः तेजः अन्नं धनं वा वयं धीमहि धारयेम». The impelling of minds is either of rites («धियः कर्माणि») or of understandings bent on dharma («धर्मादिगोचराः बुद्धीः»).

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: His last reading is meditative: the splendour is the Sun’s disc that burns away sin, «पापानां तापनं तेजो मण्डलात्मकं», held in mind, «धीमहि मनसा धारयामः», and what is taught is the supreme light standing as the Sun: «सूर्यात्मना स्थितं पारमेश्वरं तेज उपास्यत्वेन उपदिश्यते».

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: Gāyatrī metre, nominally three pādas of eight syllables; the first pāda as recited has seven (वरेण्यम् is traditionally scanned as four syllables, vareṇiyam, to make eight).

notes.label: historical
notes.text: The same verse is Ṛgveda 3.62.10, in the third maṇḍala, whose hymns are ascribed to Viśvāmitra and his family; the prayoga accordingly names Viśvāmitra as its seer.
